review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

22:1.sourceText: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.
22:1.targetText: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”

groups.note: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί ("men, brothers") is rendered Brothers.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:2.sourceText: —ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν. καὶ φησίν—
22:2.targetText: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent.  Then Paul declared,

groups.note: τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ ("in the Hebrew dialect") is rendered in Hebrew.
παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν ("they gave quiet") is rendered became … silent.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB renders the ὅτι clause as heard him speak, with no word for ὅτι ("that").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the speaker; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of φησίν.

22:3.sourceText: Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ Θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον·
22:3.targetText: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I am just as zealous for God as any of you here today.

groups.note: Ἐγώ is the subject of the whole sentence; BSB repeats I where it turns the participles πεπαιδευμένος and ὑπάρχων into new sentences.
ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος ("a Jewish man") is rendered a Jew.
The participle πεπαιδευμένος ("educated") is rendered as a new sentence.
κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν ("according to the strictness") is rendered in strict conformity to.
The adjective πατρῴου ("ancestral") is rendered of our fathers.
The noun ζηλωτής ("a zealot") is rendered zealous.
The participle ὑπάρχων ("being") is rendered as a new sentence.
The genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ ("of God") is rendered for God.
καθώς ("just as") is rendered just as … as in the comparison.
πάντες ("all") is rendered any of in the comparison.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἐστε ("you are") implied in the comparison.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds here; the Greek has only ἐστε σήμερον ("you are today").

22:4.sourceText: ὃς ταύτην τὴν Ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας,
22:4.targetText: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered I, starting a new sentence.
παραδιδούς ("handing over") is rendered throwing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for throwing; men and women are the objects of both participles.

22:5.sourceText: ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρ’ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην, ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.
22:5.targetText: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.

groups.note: The relative ὧν ("whom") is rendered them, starting a new sentence.
The participle δεξάμενος ("having received") is rendered as a finite verb.
The article τούς serves as the possessive.
εἰς Δαμασκόν ("to Damascus") goes with ἐπορευόμην; BSB places the brothers in Damascus.
The future participle ἄξων ("going to bring") expresses purpose.
τοὺς … ὄντας ("those who were") is rendered these people.
The participle δεδεμένους ("bound") is rendered as the verb apprehend.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
This καί ("also") goes with τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας ("those there too"); BSB has no word for it.
BSB does not render ἐκεῖσε ("there").

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; BSB supplies I for δεξάμενος (as Acts 23:27–30).
English joins the participle δεξάμενος, rendered obtained, to the main verb was on my way.
English joins apprehend, which renders the participle δεδεμένους, to bring.
English supplies the object of bring, referring back to these people.

22:6.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ,
22:6.targetText: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.

groups.note: The dative μοι ("to me") with the participles is rendered as the subject I.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB renders the pair πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι ("traveling and approaching") only as was approaching.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:7.sourceText: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
22:7.targetText: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’

unmappedSource.reason: The connective τε is not separately expressed in this English wording.

22:8.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην Τίς εἶ, Κύριε; εἶπέν τε πρὸς ἐμέ Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος, ὃν σὺ διώκεις.
22:8.targetText: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked.  ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.

groups.note: Ναζωραῖος ("the Nazarene") is rendered of Nazareth.

unmappedSource.reason: The connectives δέ and τε are not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB does not render πρὸς ἐμέ ("to me") after replied.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:9.sourceText: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ἐθεάσαντο, τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.
22:9.targetText: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.

groups.note: οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες ("those who were with me") is rendered My companions.
ἤκουσαν ("they heard") is rendered could … understand.
The article with the participle λαλοῦντος ("the one speaking") is rendered the One speaking.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The particle μέν, answered by δέ (but), has no English counterpart.

22:10.sourceText: εἶπον δέ Τί ποιήσω, Κύριε; ὁ δὲ Κύριος εἶπεν πρός με Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.
22:10.targetText: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’  ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’

groups.note: Κύριος ("the Lord") is rendered He.
πρός με ("to me") is rendered as the object of told.
κἀκεῖ ("and there") is rendered There.
The dative σοι ("to you") becomes the subject of the passive in English.
The dative σοι ("for you") becomes the subject of have been appointed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB renders περὶ πάντων ("about all things") as the direct object all.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle Ἀναστάς, rendered Get up, to the command go.

22:11.sourceText: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
22:11.targetText: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.

groups.note: οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ("I could not see") is rendered the brilliance … had blinded me.
χειραγωγούμενος … ἦλθον ("being led by the hand, I came") is rendered actively, my companions led me by the hand.
The article with the participle συνόντων ("those with") is rendered companions.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB makes the brilliance the subject of had blinded, so ἀπό ("because of") has no English word.
BSB renders τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου ("that light") as the light, with no word for ἐκείνου.
BSB makes the companions the subject of led, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.

22:12.sourceText: Ἀνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον, μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων,
22:12.targetText: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,

groups.note: κατὰ τὸν νόμον ("according to the law") is rendered observer of the law.
The participle μαρτυρούμενος ("being well attested") is rendered who was highly regarded.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds There, placing Ananias in Damascus.
English supplies named; the Greek has no ὄνομα ("name") here.
English adds there (Damascus); κατοικούντων means only living.

22:13.sourceText: ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον. κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.
22:13.targetText: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.

groups.note: πρὸς ἐμέ ("to me") goes with came; BSB places me after stood beside.
κἀγώ ("and I") is rendered And … I.
αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ("at that very hour") is rendered at that moment.
ἀνέβλεψα ("I looked up, I saw again") is rendered I could see.
εἰς αὐτόν ("at him") is rendered as the object of see.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render μοι ("to me") after said.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:14.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὁ Θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν Δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ,
22:14.targetText: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear His voice.

groups.note: The article ὁ is used as a pronoun ("he").
αὐτοῦ ("his") belongs to στόματος ("mouth"); BSB renders the phrase as His voice.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ("a voice from his mouth") as His voice, with no words for ἐκ τοῦ στόματος.

22:15.sourceText: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.
22:15.targetText: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.

groups.note: The dative αὐτῷ ("to him") is rendered His.
πάντας ἀνθρώπους ("all men") is rendered everyone.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves ὅτι ("for") untranslated.

22:16.sourceText: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις; ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου, ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ.
22:16.targetText: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’

groups.note: ἀπόλουσαι ("wash away") is rendered wash … away.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:17.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει
22:17.targetText: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance

groups.note: BSB renders δέ, moving the story on, as Later.
The dative μοι ("to me") with the participle is rendered as the subject I.
γενέσθαι … ἐν ἐκστάσει ("came to be in a trance") is rendered fell into a trance.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula ἐγένετο ("it came about") untranslated.
BSB does not repeat μου, the subject of the second participle; one I serves both verbs.

22:18.sourceText: καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἱερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.
22:18.targetText: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered the Lord.
ἐν τάχει ("in haste") is rendered quickly.
ἐξ Ἱερουσαλήμ ("out of Jerusalem") is rendered as the object of Leave.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence at Leave and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of παραδέξονται.

22:19.sourceText: κἀγὼ εἶπον Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·
22:19.targetText: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.

groups.note: κἀγώ ("and I") is rendered I; BSB has no word for and here.
ἐπίστανται ("they know well") is rendered know very well.
The periphrastic ἤμην φυλακίζων ("I was imprisoning") is rendered imprisoned.
Distributive κατά ("synagogue by synagogue") is rendered in one … after another.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

22:20.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.
22:20.targetText: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’

groups.note: αὐτός ("I myself") is rendered I.
The periphrastic ἤμην ἐφεστώς ("I was standing by") is rendered stood there.
συνευδοκῶν ("approving") is rendered giving … approval.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
BSB joins stood there and giving my approval without and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; the participle συνευδοκῶν has no person, and I renders αὐτός.

22:21.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.
22:21.targetText: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves ὅτι ("for") untranslated.

22:22.sourceText: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου, καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον· οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
22:22.targetText: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered by the name.
λόγου ("word") is rendered statement.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is rendered shouted.
τὸν τοιοῦτον ("such a one") is rendered him.
καθῆκεν ("it was fitting") is rendered is … fit.
αὐτόν, the subject of the infinitive ("for him to live"), is rendered He.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of Ἤκουον.
English supplies a verb; the Greek says only "until this word".
English joins the participle λέγοντες, rendered shouted, to the main verb lifted up.

22:23.sourceText: κραυγαζόντων τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα,
22:23.targetText: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,

groups.note: The article τά serves as the possessive.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves τε untranslated; the following καί is rendered and.

22:24.sourceText: ἐκέλευσεν ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν, ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.
22:24.targetText: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
The participle εἴπας ("having said") is rendered as a new sentence.
μάστιξιν ("with whips") is rendered flogged.
ἀνετάζεσθαι ("to be examined") is rendered be … interrogated.
The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
οὕτως ("thus") is rendered this.
ἐπεφώνουν ("they were shouting") is rendered outcry.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ("for what reason") as the reason for, with no word for ἥν.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins flogged, which renders μάστιξιν, to interrogated.

22:25.sourceText: ὡς δὲ προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;
22:25.targetText: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”

groups.note: τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν ("with the straps") is rendered to strap … down.
ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον ("a Roman man") is rendered a Roman citizen.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
Εἰ introduces the direct question and has no English word.
BSB has no word for καί between Roman citizen and without a trial.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of strap.
English adds there; the participle ἑστῶτα means standing.

22:26.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν λέγων Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν; ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.
22:26.targetText: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence and leaves γάρ ("for") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for hearing.
English joins the participle προσελθών, rendered went, to the main verb reported.
English supplies the object of reported.

22:27.sourceText: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Λέγε μοι, σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη Ναί.
22:27.targetText: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”  “Yes,” he answered.

groups.note: αὐτῷ ("to him"), with εἶπεν, is rendered to Paul after went.
The article ὁ is used as a pronoun ("he").

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle προσελθών, rendered went, to the main verb asked.

22:28.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.
22:28.targetText: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander.  “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.

groups.note: The article τήν serves as the possessive.
ἐκτησάμην ("I acquired") with the genitive of price is rendered paid … for.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB renders τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ("this citizenship") as my citizenship, with no word for ταύτην.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("indeed") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the complement; γεγέννημαι means only "I have been born".

22:29.sourceText: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι αὐτὸν ἦν δεδεκώς.
22:29.targetText: Then those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.

groups.note: The pronoun αὐτόν ("him") is rendered by the name.
In καὶ … δέ, καί ("even, also") marks the commander and is rendered himself.
In καὶ … δέ, δέ is the connective.
The periphrastic ἦν δεδεκώς ("he had bound") is rendered had put … in chains.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render εὐθέως ("immediately").
BSB does not render ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ("from him") after stepped back.
BSB merges ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καί ("that he is a Roman, and") into the object a Roman citizen.
BSB merges the two ὅτι clauses, so αὐτόν ("him") has no separate English word.

22:30.sourceText: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς, τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἔλυσεν αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ πᾶν τὸ συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.
22:30.targetText: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.

groups.note: τὸ ἀσφαλές ("the certainty") is rendered the real reason.
τὸ τί ("the why") is rendered reason.
καταγαγών ("having brought down") is rendered brought … down.
The one object τὸν Παῦλον serves καταγαγών and ἔστησεν; BSB gives him again with stand.
ἔστησεν ("he set") is rendered had him stand.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb endings.
English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of κατηγορεῖται.
English joins the participle καταγαγών, rendered brought down, to the main verb stand.
